name: Mao Zedong

meta.window: Spotlight on consolidation 1949-1957 (land-reform tribunals, the campaign to suppress counterrevolutionaries, the 1957 Anti-Rightist Campaign); Cultural Revolution purges 1966-1976 included for the relevant dimensions.
meta.summary: Mao Zedong led the People's Republic of China from its founding in 1949 until his death in 1976 as chairman of a one-party Communist state with no competitive elections, independent courts, or free press. His consolidation featured land-reform tribunals, the campaign to suppress counterrevolutionaries, and the 1957 Anti-Rightist Campaign, while the Cultural Revolution (1966-76) purged rivals such as Liu Shaoqi and Peng Dehuai. The Great Leap Forward famine (1959-61) killed tens of millions and is treated here as a policy catastrophe rather than documented targeted violence, given contested evidence on intent.

editor_note: Per matching discipline, the Great Leap famine is placed in competence-failures, not scored as int-02 targeted violence (intent contested). int-02 fires instead for the clearly class-targeted land-reform and zhenfan executions. The six condition/extreme indicators fire because those domains were near-totally captured under one-party rule.

scored_actions.note: Courts were subordinate to the CCP; public-security organs imposed punishments such as re-education through labor (laojiao, 1957) with no independent judicial review.
Land-reform 'people's tribunals' tried and sentenced landlords through struggle sessions outside the regular court system.
State Council provisions on re-education through labor let public-security organs impose up to 3-4 years' administrative detention without trial, bypassing due process.
No competitive national election for the head of power existed; the CCP held a one-party monopoly and the National People's Congress was indirectly selected and non-competitive.
All mass media were controlled by the CCP Central Propaganda Department; privately owned media were swept away and outlets served as instruments of 'class struggle.'

scored_actions.note: Privately owned and independent newspapers were eliminated/nationalized after the CCP took power, leaving only party-state organs such as People's Daily.

sources.title: Sixty years of news media and censorship

scored_actions.note: In the Anti-Rightist Campaign journalists were among the intellectuals branded 'rightists' and jailed or exiled to labor camps for their published criticism.
Assembly, expression, and internal movement required state approval (enforced via the hukou system and pervasive political control).

scored_actions.note: Mass detention without trial: a 1954 official report counted 1,290,000 imprisoned in the zhenfan campaign, and the laojiao camp population reached ~500,000 by 1960.
The 1951 Regulations on Punishing Counter-Revolutionaries criminalized a broad, vaguely defined category of 'counterrevolutionary' speech and activity.
One-party rule left no legislature or judiciary able to constrain the executive; the National People's Congress functioned as a rubber stamp for CCP/Mao decisions.
The state routinely imprisoned and executed people for political reasons across successive campaigns (zhenfan, Anti-Rightist, Cultural Revolution).

Systematic violence targeting a class/political group: land-reform executions of landlords and the zhenfan campaign, in which an official 1954 report cited 712,000 executed (historians argue the true toll was higher; figures contested).
Extrajudicial killings during the Cultural Revolution (Red Guard violence, local massacres, deaths in unlawful detention); total deaths estimated at 500,000-2 million (contested).

sources.title: Chronology of Mass Killings during the Chinese Cultural Revolution

scored_actions.note: Political rivals imprisoned: Marshal Peng Dehuai purged after the 1959 Lushan Conference; President Liu Shaoqi purged in 1966-68 and died in detention in 1969.
Torture in state detention: Liu Shaoqi was held in solitary confinement and subjected to regular beatings before dying in custody; violent struggle sessions were widespread.

harm.basis: The Great Leap Forward famine (~30-45 million deaths, the largest in absolute terms though famine-driven) plus campaign and Cultural Revolution deaths in the hundreds of thousands to millions. Tolls and intent are contested.

wins: Unified mainland China in 1949, ending decades of civil war, warlordism, and foreign occupation.
Land reform redistributed land to roughly 300 million peasants by 1953.
Mass literacy and public-health campaigns roughly doubled life expectancy by the mid-1970s.
Built an independent industrial and defense base; China detonated its first atomic bomb in 1964.
failures: The Great Leap Forward (1958-62) produced history's deadliest famine, ~30-45 million deaths.
The Cultural Revolution (1966-76) brought a decade of political chaos, mass purges, and economic disruption.
The Anti-Rightist Campaign (1957) branded 550,000+ intellectuals as 'rightists,' gutting professional expertise.
The Hundred Flowers reversal and serial purges destroyed institutional trust and human capital.
